title: Spinal Cord Blood Flow Measurement
official: A Hemodynamic Neuroprotection Paradigm for Spinal Cord Injury
summary: The purpose of this study is to measure spinal cord blood flow in participants with acute cervical or high-thoracic spinal cord injury. During planned spinal cord decompression surgery after acute spinal cord injury, participants will have a blood flow sensor placed around the area of injury. The participant's breathing rate and depth, which is controlled via a ventilator as part of standard surgical care, will be manipulated to test whether progressively increasing carbon dioxide levels increases spinal cord blood flow. This will provide the first safety data of the effects of altering carbon dioxide intraoperatively for spinal cord injury.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18-70 presenting with acute SCI between C4-T6
* Requiring surgical decompression, with or without instrumentation
* Able to be mechanically ventilated under general anaesthesia for the surgical procedure
* Able to provide informed consent, or with a legally authorized/substitute decision-maker able to provide consent where the participant has impaired capacity in the acute setting, with ongoing consent obtained from the participant following completion of the surgical procedure. Enrollment occurs in the acute setting where capacity may be temporarily impaired

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known or suspected traumatic brain injury
* Severe multi-systemic injury or chest trauma
* Hemodynamically unstable, or otherwise ineligible for surgery
* Confirmed pregnancy
* Any other condition that, in the judgment of the attending clinical team or investigators, would make participation unsafe
